newsitem.title: INDIA: India's IOC owes ONGC 11 bln rupees-paper.
newsitem.headline: India's IOC owes ONGC 11 bln rupees-paper.

text.p: Indian Oil Corp (IOC) owes Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) 11 billion rupees ($307 million) for crude purchases made between November and April, the Financial Express daily reported on Monday.
The paper said deferred payment on the purchases was sought for six months, but so far IOC had repaid between 4.0 and 5.0 billion rupees, leaving 11 billion outstanding.

Indian oil companies are facing a credit crunch while the government deliberates how to repay them for selling products below market prices to support subsidies on some petroleum products, like diesel and kerosene.
The government owed the companies 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) from the oil pool account deficit at the end of March, and the bill has continued rising.
Other refiners have been unable to pay IOC, the sole importer of crude oil into India, on time for feedstock, and IOC has fallen behind on its payments to the domestic crude supplier ONGC.
IOC is owed more than 90 billion rupees from the oil pool account, and has had to borrow heavily to keep crude supplies flowing.
The daily said the latest IOC borrowing was a $1.0 billion foreign exchange facility syndicated by Bank of America and ABN Amro.
India's United Front coalition government's steering committee meets on Tuesday to discuss how to reduce the oil pool deficit, by raising domestic product prices and other measures. ($1=35.76 rupees)
